sections.html:
Brighton reaches into both Adams and Weld counties and serves as the Adams County seat. In 2020, 39,718 of its 40,083 residents lived on the Adams side. Population has kept rising: 43,473 in a 2024 estimate, then 45,395 for July 1, 2025, with a median age of 33.9.

Before anything else, find out which county your lot sits in. That county sends the tax bill and files the deed, and your latest tax statement names it. Most Brighton houses fall under Adams.

New homes are going up while resale houses sit on the market, and a growing city also attracts investors and buyers who like to renovate. So a house with problems can still find a taker.

sections.h2: Property tax due dates in Adams County
sections.html:
Adams County gives Brighton owners two ways to pay: one lump sum, or two halves.

Payment optionDue dateRule
First halfFebruary 28Half payments only, no partial amounts
Second halfJune 15Bills of $25 or less cannot be split
Full paymentApril 30Postmark by the due date counts

Anything postmarked late picks up delinquent interest. Because the county bills one year in arrears, the figure you settle at closing reflects last year's value and rates, not this year's.

sections.h2: Unpaid taxes and the lien sale
sections.html:
Late-payment notices are mailed in July. If a balance stays open, the county advertises it and then holds an online tax lien sale, running October 7 through November 6. Paying by 5:00 PM on October 31 keeps you clear of the sale-related interest and fees.

Selling does not erase an old balance. It comes out of your proceeds at closing, which is why it pays to request an exact payoff early. The county's Adams County due dates page has the details.

Part of Brighton is in Weld County, and Weld bills those parcels. If that is your situation, phone the Weld County treasurer for payment dates and a payoff figure. The deed goes to Weld County for recording instead of Adams. The rest of the sale looks the same.

sections.h2: Contractor license rules before you renovate
sections.html:
The city wants a contractor license for general, mechanical, plumbing and electrical jobs, but owners who work on their own home are exempt. The exemption covers a personal residence and its accessory buildings, and an owner may build only one personal residence in any three consecutive years.

Each license lasts twelve months, cannot be transferred, and comes with a proof-of-insurance requirement. Roofing, concrete flatwork, framing and drywall belong to the Class E specialty trades license. Brighton also has a Minor Home Repairs Program, and its code enforcement staff are listed under Community Development.

Think about this before you spend money on pre-sale fixes. A hired contractor needs the proper license, permits have to be pulled, and inspections have to pass. The city also cautions that moving into a space before the certificate of occupancy exists can jeopardize the contractor's license. An as-is sale avoids all of it.

sections.h2: Winter wear on a Brighton house
sections.html:
Winters here are cold and semi-arid, with about 34.5 inches of snow in a typical year. Freeze and thaw cycles are harder on a house than rainfall is. Inspectors working for buyers tend to check:

  • how old the roof is, plus flashing and gutters
  • the age of the furnace and water heater
  • window seals and attic insulation
  • hairline cracks in concrete and stucco

Deferred work in any of those places can sink a financed deal. A cash buyer who takes the house as is does not ask you to fix it first.

Few sellers here have a single problem. More often it is some combination of timing, repairs and paperwork:

  • a house inherited in Adams or Weld County that needs probate or a trust transfer before it can be sold
  • an aging roof, furnace or set of pipes after many Front Range winters
  • a tenant living there under a lease that must be dealt with
  • a mortgage that is behind, or back taxes

Listing the traditional way brings showings, a buyer's inspection and the risk of an appraisal gap. A cash purchase usually has no lender, so you can pick the closing day. Whichever path you take, get the Adams or Weld tax figure from the title company before settling on a date.

sections.h2: Selling with a probate or trust step
sections.html:
When a house comes through an estate, the paperwork has to catch up with the title before a deed can be signed. Tell the title company at the start that probate or a trust transfer is involved, and give them the names of everyone who must sign. That one conversation usually does more for your timeline than anything about the house.

If heirs live out of town, say so as well, since signing can often be arranged from a distance. Keep copies of any trust documents or court papers where you can find them quickly, because the title company will ask for them before it can schedule anything.

An inherited house that nobody wants to maintain is a common reason to choose a cash sale, since the heirs avoid repairs, showings and months of carrying costs while the paperwork moves.

Once you accept an offer, the title company becomes the center of the deal. It searches the record for liens, confirms what is owed on the parcel with the right treasurer, prepares the deed and sets the closing statement. That statement shows how the current year's tax is divided and what, if anything, is paid off from your proceeds.

Read it line by line before you sign. If a number surprises you, ask where it came from. A cash sale has fewer lines than a financed one, because there is no lender fee and no appraisal charge, but the tax split and recording still appear.

sections.h2: How a cash sale of a Brighton house goes
sections.html:
1. Describe the property to us and we look it over.
  2. You get a written offer that treats the house as it stands.
  3. Pick a title company and a closing date that suit you.
  4. The deed is filed in the county where your parcel lies, Adams or Weld.
  5. Proceeds reach you at closing.

An offer you decline costs nothing, and you are free to set it beside a listing or another investor's number first.

Bring the tax bill, any mortgage statement and the names on the title. Those papers, more than the condition of the house, tend to decide how fast closing happens.

faqs.q: Which county do I deal with if I sell a house in Brighton, CO?
faqs.a: It depends on the parcel. Brighton sits in Adams and Weld counties, and most residents are on the Adams side. Your tax bill shows which county covers your house.

faqs.q: When is the second-half property tax payment due in Brighton?
faqs.a: June 15 for Adams County parcels. The first half is due February 28 and a full payment is due April 30.

faqs.q: Do I need a contractor license to fix up my own Brighton house?
faqs.a: An owner working on a personal residence and its accessory buildings is excepted from the city's contractor license rule, though permits and inspections still apply. Hired contractors generally need a city license and proof of insurance.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Brighton house as is?
faqs.a: Yes. A cash sale as is means you do not repair or update the property for a buyer's lender or inspection. Ask for the offer in writing and review it with your title company.

faqs.q: Does the county tax bill change when I sell?
faqs.a: The bill follows the property, and Adams County collects taxes one year in arrears. The closing statement normally divides the tax between you and the buyer, so ask the title company how it was figured.
